quote.text: In every walk with nature, one receives far more than he seeks.
quote.author: John Muir

fun_fact.text: Hummingbirds are the only birds that can fly backwards! Their wings beat in a figure-eight pattern, allowing them to hover in place and even fly upside down for short distances. A hummingbird's heart can beat up to 1,260 times per minute.

short_read.title: The Secret Lives of Tide Pools
short_read.teaser: Tide pools along the Pacific coast are like tiny worlds, home to colorful sea stars, hermit crabs, and anemones. Learn how these remarkable creatures survive the rhythm of the tides.

medium_read.title: The Magyar Migrations: How Hungarians Found Their Home
medium_read.teaser: The story of how the Hungarian people journeyed from the Ural Mountains to settle in the heart of Europe over a thousand years ago is a fascinating tale of adventure and survival. Discover the origins of Hungarian culture and language.

long_read.title: The Return of Wolves to the Olympic Peninsula
long_read.teaser: After nearly a century of absence, gray wolves are slowly returning to the Olympic Peninsula, bringing both wonder and complexity to the ecosystem. This is the story of their journey home and what it means for the forests you love.

port_angeles.title: Deer in the Garden
port_angeles.description: August is prime time to spot black-tailed deer around Port Angeles, especially in the early morning and evening hours. These gentle browsers are native to the Olympic Peninsula and can often be seen near the edges of forests and meadows, even occasionally wandering through residential gardens at Park View Villas!

puzzle_1.question: A hummingbird visits about ___ flowers per day to find enough nectar for energy.
puzzle_1.correct_response: Wonderful! Yes, these tiny dynamos visit around 1,000 flowers every day — what incredible energy!
puzzle_1.close_response: You're very close! These busy little birds actually visit about 1,000 flowers daily to fuel their amazing flight.
puzzle_1.wrong_response: These tireless little fliers visit about 1,000 flowers each day! That's a lot of gardens to explore.
puzzle_1.learn_more_text: Hummingbirds need to consume half their body weight in sugar daily and can visit over 1,000 flowers to meet their energy needs. Their metabolism is so fast they must eat every 10-15 minutes!

puzzle_2.question: Which Hungarian word means 'thank you'?
puzzle_2.correct_response: Köszönöm! That's right, Ildiko — a beautiful word you know well!
puzzle_2.wrong_response: The answer is 'köszönöm' — such a warm and essential Hungarian word! (Szia means hello, igen means yes, and viszlát means goodbye.)
puzzle_2.learn_more_text: Hungarian is a unique language from the Finno-Ugric family, unrelated to most European languages. It's known for its beautiful sounds and complex grammar with 18 grammatical cases.

puzzle_3.question: What type of marine mammal is commonly spotted in the Strait of Juan de Fuca near Port Angeles?
puzzle_3.correct_response: Yes! Orcas are regular visitors to the Strait, including both resident pods that eat salmon and transient orcas that hunt seals. What a privilege to live where these magnificent creatures swim!
puzzle_3.wrong_response: The answer is orcas! These magnificent black and white whales swim through the Strait regularly, and you might spot them from the shore on a lucky day. Sea lions do visit too, but orcas are the most iconic.
puzzle_3.learn_more_text: The Southern Resident orcas are an endangered population that frequents the Strait of Juan de Fuca, following salmon runs. The best viewing months are often May through September.
